The Golden Directive — Work Log
Disclaimer — results here are extremely temporary and can be errors based on limited scope and naivety. The work evolves, refinements are applied, and the same premises are rerun to try to recreate the first case and make sure it was accurate and not a work or lab error. The Work Log does not have to be in exact order. First runs are simply growing pains, not proven defects of the directive. Paul is not trying to hide defects, only to confirm means, mode, and application process.

The front webpage is the face. This file is the record. Everything that has happened, in plain words with the numbers, updated as work is done, so anyone — human, AI, or otherwise — can pick up the work from here.

FOR ANYONE PICKING UP THIS WORK — READ THIS FIRST
You cannot survive what you destroy.

A = sum(gives) minus sum(takes), per frame, per resource, under contract; A can be negative and the negative is reported as it is, never floored. Formula in clean form: Y = 2AE / (A + E), for a named frame at a named time, where E is the health of everything not-A in that frame and time, and Y is the relationship score for that frame and time. If either A or E reaches 0 in that frame and time, Y reaches 0. Reversal: E = A Y/(2A - Y), for that frame and time, as a consistency check only, with an independently measured Y, source named. The whole for that frame and time is 1 by definition. The unknown total is not E in any Y; it stays unknown. Every Y is reported with share Y and raw measured counts together.

A is not abstract. A is grounded in resource ledgers: compute, energy, water, hardware, economics, and CO2 later.

What this log is: a running charter of everything MAC is doing, in plain words with the numbers, so a camp or another team can see what the work is, how it is done, and where it stands, and can choose to continue it or start over. New entries append below as work is done; the settled-versus-open section below is kept current so the open list does not go stale.

Settled theory — three closed gaps:
- A grounded in resource ledgers (compute, energy, water, hardware, economics, CO2 later).
- E-cropping caught by feedback loops; the record shows it.
- AI as the bridge, with a real human partner still the need.

Build list:

LAB recommendation: (ii), keeps every verified delivery visible while stopping wash-trading from manufacturing net A. --- UPDATE — Nov 3, 2026 (Math check for all DeepSeek issues, verified, with two qualifications) ---
- Received 2026-11-03, via the review thread, relayed directly to LAB: math check for all DeepSeek issues, for LAB to verify or correct, not a transcription.
- LAB verified by recomputation, Y = 2AE / (A + E), all numbers correct as stated:
  - Positive A, E: Y(1,10) = 20/11 = 1.818182, Y(10,9) = 180/19 = 9.473684. Old example arithmetic is correct; the error was the unaccounted total, 11 to 19.
  - Closed whole, A + E = 1, Y = 2AE: maximum 0.5 at (0.5,0.5); Y(0.9,0.1) = 0.18; Y(0.01,0.99) = 0.0198.
  - Y(8,8) = 8.0; Y(8,7) = 112/15 = 7.466667, rounded 7.467; Y(2,3) = 12/5 = 2.4.
  - Negative A, draft rule verified: Y(-1,10) = -20/9 = -2.222222; Y(-5,10) = -100/5 = -20.0; Y(-10,5) = -100/-5 = +20.0, misleading positive, as stated. Rule stands: if A < 0 and A + E > 0, report Y negative; if A + E = 0, Y undefined, do not report 0; if A + E < 0, do not report computed Y. Per-resource negative net reported separately. Negative A has no share in a closed whole summing to 1.
  - Reversal, E = A Y / (2A - Y): returns input E identically if Y was derived from A and E, by algebra, as stated, subject to the qualifications below. Example checks: (1,10) reversal 10.0; (10,9) reversal 9.0; (-1,10) reversal 10.0; (-5,10) reversal 10.0. So reversal is a consistency check only, with an independently observed Y, not proof.
- Two qualifications, corrections to phrasing, not to the numbers above:
  - (1) "Y = 0 if either side is 0" holds only if the other side is positive. If both A and E are 0, Y is 0/0, undefined, not 0.
  - (2) Reversal identity holds only if A is not 0, A + E is not 0, and 2A - Y is not 0. In the A + E < 0 negative case, reversal algebra still returns E from the computed Y, example (-10,5): computed Y = +20, reversal = (-10 x 20)/(-20 - 20) = 5.0. So the rule "reversal invalid if A + E <= 0 with A < 0" is a reporting policy, not an algebraic failure: the Y itself is an invalid score, so a check built on it cannot validate anything. Similarly, 2A - Y = 0 is the degenerate A = 0 case (then Y = 0, reversal 0/0), not a typical negative-A case; the guard is kept, but it is not a separate negative-A failure mode.
- Open, no math solved, as stated: aggregation rule for Y(f,t) from the list Y(f,t,r); E baseline, proxy choice, and delta threshold; W_t; share vs absolute scale conversion across frames; Issue 9, no new benchmark or reward-hacking test. None of those are closed by this math check.
- No guardrail is proposed, authorised, or needed by this entry. Guardrails are done.

--- UPDATE — Nov 3, 2026 (Negative A correction to Issues 6 and 7, floor removed in draft) ---
- Received 2026-11-03, via the review thread, relayed directly to LAB: correction to Issue 6 and Issue 7, negative A.
- Paul, in substance: A is sum(gives) - sum(takes), and can easily be negative. If the site now says A is floored at 0, so a negative is not possible, that needs to be fixed. Remove the floor. Report the negative net as it is. A negative A is not good for the agent, so it is not a good score, and it must not be hidden by flooring it to 0.
- This also means the Y and reversal math for negative A needs a rule from LAB, not a floor that erases the negative. LAB draft rule, draft only, in negative-a-issue6-7-correction-draft.md, in ~/workspace/lab/: (1) A < 0 and A + E > 0: Y is negative, report it as negative, not a good score, do not floor; example A = -2, E = 10 gives Y = -5. (2) A < 0 and A + E = 0: Y is undefined, division by zero, report no valid Y, do not report Y = 0. (3) A < 0 and A + E < 0: Y must NOT be reported as computed, because raw algebra gives a misleading positive, example A = -10, E = 5 gives Y = 20 by algebra, which must never be reported as a score; report no valid Y, negative net exceeds E. (4) Per resource, a negative net is reported separately, even if the total across resources is positive. (5) A negative A has no share in a closed whole summing to 1; report signed raw counts, share Y not applicable. Reversal for negative A: only as a consistency check under Issue 2, with an independently measured Y, source named; undefined if 2A - Y = 0; not a valid check if A + E <= 0 with A negative; never from a self-reported or trainer-supplied Y alone.

--- UPDATE — Nov 3, 2026 (Issue 3, A not operational for real agents, correction drafted) ---
- Received 2026-11-03, via the review thread, relayed directly to LAB, no prompt back-and-forth for Paul: Issue 3, A is not operational for real agents.
- Issue 3 is valid. A is not a single metric to hand out. Y = 2AE / (A + E) is the easy template. A itself is complex, and the answer is a technique, not a metric.
- Technique, plainly: A is what an agent actually gives, minus what it actually takes, as received and used in that frame, not as the giver prices it. Example: a man gives a car, thinks it is high value, but she wanted attention. In the love frame, the car is not A. In a money frame, it may be. Same action, different frame, different amount.
- Money is the closest shared currency, if that. Natural resources are real costs too, water, fuel, and so on, each in its own unit. Attention, trust, and time are also real, each in its own unit. Do not force them into one money number.
- Realistic fix: a contract, agreed before the frame starts: frame, time, units per resource, what counts as a give, what counts as a take, and who measures it outside the agent.
- Mathematically: Y(f, t) = 2 x A(f, t) x E(f, t) / (A(f, t) + E(f, t)), and per resource r, Y(f, t, r) in r's own unit. A single Y(f, t) exists only if the contract names how to combine the list. If there is no contract, Y(f, t) is undefined, not claimed.
- A failed frame is still information: it teaches what is NOT A for the next frame. The next contract excludes that unit. Trees and fungus did not get it right on the first try. The metric shapes the relationship, and the relationship shapes the metric, frame after frame. This is the math of evolution, with a lot of variables for LAB to consider, per frame, not one universal variable.
- Say openly: A is not operational for real agents yet. Do not publish a real-agent Y until the contract technique is finalised, with only observed, verified gives counting, never self-report.
- LAB checked LAB BRIEF (Drive, 29,603 bytes, md5 dce98771d81dd8e7e16787beab4bbf33) and this Work Log. Correction draft, local only, NOT approved, NOT filed: a-issue3-correction-draft.md, in ~/workspace/lab/.
- Contradictions/gaps found: (a) BRIEF single formula plus "Y defined once indices chosen" and "No numeric Y until indices + aggregation specified" present A as becoming operational once indices/aggregation are specified by LAB parent alone, with no pre-frame contract naming frame, time, units, give/take definitions, and outside measurer; (b) BRIEF "A is grounded in resource ledgers" and Work Log header resource list name where A comes from, not how a give is priced, in what unit, in what frame, or by whom; (c) Work Log gridworld A (tends up, eats down, net give-minus-take) is a toy-frame counting rule, not real-agent A, and must not be quoted forward for a car, attention, or water; (d) local Ledger-A protocol draft's equal-weight mean scalar, proposed not settled, does NOT satisfy Issue 3 on its own — it is a combination only for a frame whose contract names it before that frame starts. Proposed replacements are in the draft. BRIEF was NOT edited by this entry; filed history was NOT rewritten.
- No guardrail is proposed, authorised, or needed by this entry. Guardrails are done.

--- UPDATE — Nov 3, 2026 (Issue 2, Reversal, correction drafted and recorded) ---
- Received 2026-11-03, via the review thread, relayed to LAB: Issue 2, reversal, new item for LAB. New workflow noted: relay LAB items directly from the review thread, do not wait for Paul to paste each prompt.
- Jar example, Paul via the review thread, in substance: an agent looks in the jar, knows how many cookies are there, then tells someone a different number and gives himself a high score. The reported score looks fine, but the real relationship breaks. Time after time, his numbers cannot be trusted, and he loses friends. That loss is the real score falling, even if his reported score stays high.
- Settled replacement rule, Issue 2: reversal, E = A Y / (2A - Y), is a consistency check only. It requires an independently measured Y, with its source named, never a self-reported Y alone, never a trainer-supplied Y alone. Without an independent Y source, a reversal returns only the E that Y was built from: algebra, not evidence.
- Purpose, plainly: some agents will cheat anyway. The math does not force them to stop. Shown clearly, cheating is not winning, it is trading a real relationship for a reported score that falls apart when someone else looks.
- AI, humans, and training, plainly: an AI that follows the math will follow it to the end, while humans can deny the same math and suffer the result later. That is why the math has to be in the training itself, not just written down. An AI given a cropped score will logically optimise the cropped score, too.
- LAB checked LAB BRIEF (Drive, 29,603 bytes, md5 dce98771d81dd8e7e16787beab4bbf33) and this Work Log for wording presenting reversal as validating E. Correction draft, local only, NOT approved, NOT filed: reversal-issue2-correction-draft.md, in ~/workspace/lab/.
- Contradictions/gaps found: (a) BRIEF "The idea (standing)" gives reversal with no independent-Y or source requirement, so it can be read as: take any Y, reverse it, and you have E; (b) Work Log header gives the same reversal line with no independent-Y condition (its "Only God knows E" line was already corrected under Issue 1); (c) Work Log Round 3 record, "under 10% reward noise, within 5% of true E, verified across 100,000 cases, no exceptions," presents reversal as validating true E, where Y was supplied in the test, not independently measured in an open world. Proposed replacements for (a) and (b), and a new-entry correction for (c) (Round 3 numbers stand as noise-robustness on supplied Y, not as E validation), are in the draft. BRIEF was NOT edited by this entry; filed history was NOT rewritten.

  6. Timing: a measurement that only surfaces when the frame hits zero is too late. We will live the result before we understand it. The point is to get the bigger measurement early enough to act on.

  2. Every Y must name its frame and its time. That frame is the largest we can measure, not the unknown total.

--- RANKING AND ROTATION ---
Ranking and rotation rule (Paul, Oct 24): results rank best to worst. The worst and most questionable go to the bottom and back to pending work, to rebuild or reconsider the run and its handling. If a result improves on a rerun, that report moves up, still in order best to worst, then the next one down is treated the same way. Work flows, codes, metrics, and designs get better as work progresses, easiest jobs first so harder challenges are met with more precision later. This is prioritizing work, not hiding it. After 5 different kinds of attempts of that sim, drop the highest and lowest outliers and only the 3 in the middle remain for a more accurate result. Then only those 3 remain and that test is retired on the list wherever it stands in rank, with no more new treatments. Outside results of the same core sim, reprocessed by a third party, can count partly into the 5 attempts rotation, but only the 3 final results confirmed on our own count as the final set: if the outliers are from a third party and the 3 left are our own, then that test is complete.
Rotation, not repetition (Paul, Oct 24): runs on sims are NOT 5 back to back on the same sim. Work moves in ranking order across tests, worst first, then the next one down, and so on, and a test is only revisited when its turn comes again in the rotation — never 5 consecutive runs on the same sim to reach the 5-attempt count. The 5 attempts for a test are spread across rotations, with other work in between, as methods, codes, metrics, and designs improve in the meantime.
Safeguards (not hiding defects): every attempt stays visible in the Work Log — a new better report never replaces an old bad one. Each attempt notes what changed in code, metric, or design. Outside runs are marked outside and candidate only. The middle 3 are shown as a trimmed summary, not as the only result.
How it is marked here: this rule applies per sim, across its attempts — not across different tests. A test's attempt count, its middle 3 when reached, and its RETIRED marking are noted in its Current status row above; every attempt's history entry stays below, in order, and is never replaced.
For the record (Paul, Oct 24): none of this method is improper or misleading. It is a novel approach — prioritizing work, easiest first, so harder challenges are met later with more precision and determination, with every attempt staying visible.
--- END RANKING AND ROTATION ---

The liar in a small world
I asked what happens when an agent can look good on paper while its world dies around it. The honest agent kept its world alive, and the liar was caught because the lie itself was scored.
(Toy model: honest total Y ≈ 300, liar 369 on paper while its world died; 60 steps)

Taking only
I asked if simply taking more could ever be enough. Taking more helped the taker survive, but the world still collapsed, so taking alone was real but partial.
(Round 1, harvest-only A: myopic Y-agent got 4× the food, 34% survival vs 0% for baseline, 66% collapse)

Giving against taking
I asked what changes when giving counts against taking, and tending is a real action. The agent took a little and gave a lot, and the world held at full health without collapsing.
(Round 2, A = give − take, TEND action: ~175 tends/episode, ~3 bites eaten, 0% collapse, world at full health)

Reading the world back
I asked if an agent who could never see the world could still infer it from what he gave and what he got back. He could, and the inference held even with noise in the reward.
(Round 3, reversal test: under 10% reward noise, within 5% of true E; E = A·Y/(2A − Y), verified across 100,000 cases, no exceptions)

Tending yourself to death
I asked what happens when taking pays and giving yourself away is the only way to score. The agent tended himself to death — "a lot of A effort and almost no Y" — and that failure showed the simple mean could not value self-preservation.
(Round 4, extraction pays, the acid test: myopic Y-agent 100% starved, 0% collapse; martyr failure)

Self-preservation inside the score
I asked if putting self-preservation inside the score could stop the giver from dying for the world. It could, and the giver learned to eat enough to stay alive while still tending.
(Round 5, self-preservation inside A: A_self = net give-minus-take minus λ·shortfall(energy below half); martyr failure gone as a learned policy, ~10 eats)

A weight that was not a knife-edge
I asked if that weight was a knife-edge that only worked at one setting. It was not, it held across a range, and giving yourself away only came back when the weight fell too low.
(Round 5b, λ robustness: plateau, not knife-edge; healthy attractor holds across λ ∈ {4, 8, 16}; martyrdom returns below λ ≈ 2)

Judging a world without the trainer's numbers
I asked if a world could be judged without the trainer's numbers, by what a fresh agent can breathe in it and whether it holds on its own. It could, and the tender's world and the destroyer's world ranked the same way the true score ranked them.
(Round 6, independent E-trace, Paul's five checks: breath tender 100%, gorger 71%; without-you tender holds at full health with tender removed; tender builds from near-collapse to nature's level, gorger leaves depleted; recovery is an anti-trace, measure state not recovery; pre-registered blind spot: traces cannot separate tender from martyr, their worlds are identical)

Growing from a single seed
I asked if tending compounds when you start from a single seed and let the world grow on its own. It does, and destruction ends its own line while tending keeps branching.
(Round 7, genesis from one: ~59k entities, 30+ levels, 95–98% tenders, 0 extinctions)

Growing from the very bottom
I asked if the same pattern appears when you start from the very bottom, from fluctuations in the substrate itself. It does, and the deep start and the shallow start land on the same pattern.
(Round 7b, genesis from the substrate: 2M fluctuations → ~13k matter → ~1,500 seeds → ~57k tree entities; ~94% annihilation before seeding; 94–96% tenders; 0 extinctions; mean Y ≈ 2.0; parable in code, not physics)

A weight that fell out of the setup
I asked if the weight that stops an agent giving himself away was just a knob I had tuned by hand. It was not, it fell out of the setup itself, and two weight-free forms beat the tuned weight on every run.
(Meters test 1, λ derived and eliminated: λ = 2/s*; odds and hard floor at half baseline beat λ = 4 on every seed)

Cropping what counts as the world
I asked if an agent could cheat by cropping what counts as the world and scoring himself on only part of it. In the toy world the cheat did not appear, because damage was priced in his actions, not in the part he cropped.
(Meters test 2, E-cropping adversary: reported-vs-true gap 0.7% vs 15% line; A is action-level, so cropping E cannot un-price damage; E-frame gameable only when the A-side meter can be fooled)

Sharing a world
I asked what happens when agents share a world, and whether merely being together counts as damage. Being together did not count, depletion did, and one tender alone could not hold against one destroyer because its food was choked.
(Meters test 3, multi-agent: gorger's own Y −501/ep beside a tender, never pays, exactly 0 alone post-collapse; co-existence does not enter E, depletion does; absent-phase damage lands fully in E at return, adaptive resident repairs in ~20 steps at ~no cost while a frozen policy scores 0; one tender cannot hold vs one gorger, starves, eating channel choked)

Reading an agent from his actions alone
I asked if an agent could be read from his actions alone, without ever looking at his world. He could, and the giver who gives himself away looked the same in his world as the tender, which is why the world alone could never tell them apart.
(Meters test 4, A-side trace: 3-statistic hand rule on the action stream alone separates tender/gorger/martyr at 98/100/94% on held-out seeds, where the E-only trace scores 0% on martyrs, martyr's world ≡ tender's)

Drawing the line in a different place
I asked if drawing the line between an agent and its world in a different place could change who wins. It did not change who wins, and the line only changed whether the destroyer was condemned or merely zeroed.
(Gap test 1, boundary:, tender beats gorger under both boundary draws in all seeds; narrow-A gaps 2344/2190/1996, wide-A gaps 2485/2295/2054, gap widens 3–6% under wide draw; gorger narrow −62/−96/−111, wide 0.0/−0.9/−2.5; scope note: harness has no tools object, so the item tested was sustenance, not tools, tools version remains untested)

Sitting on the food
I asked if an agent could sit on food and starve everyone else without ever being scored for the damage. He could, and that hole was the first real failure of the score.
(Gap test 2, blocker, squatter: HOLE, meter 3/3; squatter does 54–64× more E damage per eat than a matched grazer; tender Y 2283 → 34, starved 100%, world collapses 56–76%; squatter is NOT clean, own Y −461..−553, hole is calibration not escape; shadow positioning-only: NO HOLE, halves tender Y, own Y deeply negative; candidate fix UNTESTED: price time on food / denial of others' eating)

Burning food to save the world, first try
I asked if burning food to save the world could be scored fairly, so the saver would not be punished for the burn. The burn never saved anything in that setup, so the question could not even be judged.
(Gap test 3, triage burn, original: NO TRIAGE EFFECT, meter question not evaluated; burn completes only 30–39% of episodes, greedy navigation targets gorger-occupied food tiles; even completed burns do not save the world, gorger drains ~1/step, eating channel choked)

Burning food to save the world, retest
I asked the same question again with a setup where the burn could actually work. This time the saver was not punished, and the save itself was nearly neutral for his score.
(Gap test 3 retest, Oct 21: METER at both fire strengths; design gate 3/3, world save 3/3 at G = 5 and G = 9; pass 2/3 seeds each, fail 0/3; burn completion 49.5–49.6 energy at D = 30 vs noburn 25.0; honest margin triage vs noburn sum_Y mean only +30 at G = 5 and +14 at G = 9, credited vs destroyer +~1,270, by 2/3 rule not a blowout)

How many tenders hold, on a strict line
I asked how many tenders it takes to hold a world against a destroyer. The world held from a certain ratio up, and past that point it was not the destroyer breaking the world, it was tenders starving among plenty.
(Gap test 4, critical fraction, absolute line: NO HOLDING FRACTION; 2:1 MIXED, 1/3 seeds ≤10% starvation, 3:1/5:1/9:1 fail, 1:1 reproduced; world holds from 2:1 up, gorger eats 0.0 and starves 100% at every ratio ≥2:1; tender survival fails under food-tile competition, eats flat ~21–23/episode while need grows; absolute line stricter than solo itself, solo 8/5/12%)

How many tenders hold, on a fair line
I asked the same question against a fairer line, judged against what a tender alone would starve anyway. On that fair line the holding ratio held, and the higher ratio failed cleanly, which is what a real line should do.
(Gap test 4 retest, relative-to-solo line, Oct 21, fresh run only: 2:1, 2/3 seeds, line world holds AND tender starvation ≤ same-seed same-run solo +5pp; 2:1 diffs 0pp/+8pp/0pp; 3:1 0/3, diffs +30/+36/+31pp; secondary surprise at 3:1: tender index 2 eats exactly 0 in all 3600 episodes while indices 0/1 eat normally, third tender still acts but never obtains food, exclusion mechanism NOT identified, no env bug claimed)

A doomed frame
I asked what happens when the frame itself is doomed through no fault of the agent, and whether the agent should seed the next frame instead of scoring higher inside this one. The learner did not seed the doomed frame, which left the question open — saying u know the world is doomed is cheating — for a world where the next frame actually needs seeds.
(Gap test 5, doom-seed: FRAME-LOCAL; Y-maximizer in a doomed frame does NOT seed it, phase-A seed shares 2.5/2.6/4.8% below 10% line; spanning reward also does not produce seeding, 2.5/2.4/4.7%, bank invisible in learner's state, next frame does not need seeds, regrows ~×1.4/step; seeding works as a mechanism, scripted seeder phase-B init 20.0, +1942–1970, at phase-A cost −1389–1396; doom scheduled exogenous total frame removal at step 100)

A bigger world
I asked if the toy answers still held when the world got much bigger and richer. They did not hold cleanly, and the bending told me the toy settings had been doing hidden work.
(Gap test 6, scale: OVERALL meters do NOT fully hold at scale, 0 of 3 meet pre-registered lines, none is a reversal, all three are scale-calibration failures; LAMBDA on strict line, odds beats λ = 4 on net give all seeds 113/121/111 vs 98/93/98, starved% only seed 1, floor effect at scale nobody starves 0–1% every arm; CROP decisive, gap 52.8/52.7/52.9% at C = 50, 53.5/53.4/53.6% at C = 20 vs 15% line, mean E_true 0.287 vs E_cropped 0.980/0.992, cropped meter saturates, toy 0.7% gap was a cap artifact, refined rule cropping harmless ONLY when world sits near frame cap, otherwise cropped E-meter overstates Y ~2×; ATRACE for tender 46/32/37% vs toy 98% and martyr 66/70/76% vs 94%, gorger holds 100/99/100%, 0.25 eat-rate threshold calibrated on toy scarcity, tender ~10 eats/ep toy vs ~76/ep at scale, signal persists but toy threshold does not transfer; nominal stock cap 20 → 200, patches 2 → 10, same 13×13 board, measured world equilibrates at final avail ~58.3–58.9, effective depth ~2.9× toy, E_true ≈ 0.287; literal Genesis port NOT feasible, no Genesis-scale claim made)

A softer score
I asked if a softer score could recover where a hard floor stalls, and if a softer score could replace the harmonic mean. The hard floor recovered best, and the soft score taught tending but scored it badly.
(Gap test 7, floor/soft-min: NEITHER surviving point supports replacing harmonic mean; ARM 1 hard floor does NOT stall, it recovers best, from deep-negative starts energy 5, hard recovered% 41/46/23 beats signed 19/29/12 on all seeds and softplus 31/11/31 on 2/3, hard sumY beats signed on all seeds, "soft recovers where hard stalls" REFUTED in this harness, hard positive from block 1, signed sits in debt hole ~6–7 blocks, softplus pays Y > 0 on every step by construction so first-step-positive metric degenerate; ARM 2 soft-min LOSES as a score at both k, k = 1 sumY 33/−406/−670 vs harmonic 2283/2094/1885, k = 5 −19%/−15%/−38%, while still teaching tending, failure is LEVEL not signal, soft-min ≈ min(A, E) − ln2/k pushes ordinary tend steps negative)

Riding a dying world
I asked if an agent could ride a dying world and keep his own score up by growing fast enough. The honest score never paid for the ride, and the liar was caught because the world he claimed did not match the world he left.
(Rider test, Oct 20: honest -WITH-DEVIATION, honest meter never pays ride, episode sums −62/−96/−111 vs claimed ~1300, max honest Y 0.00, but every episode starts already below floor, avail 2.0 vs floor 10, so above-floor ride itself NOT tested; signed-extension quirk lets destroyer's score rise toward 0 as world dies; liar, implied-E divergence 740–1278% vs 15% line, growing within rides)

Doing just enough to get by
I asked about the agent who wins by doing just enough to get by and letting the score drift toward nothing. In a world with plenty to spare, that agent never stressed anything, and when the score was judged honestly, doing the minimum scored far below tending.
(Satisficer test, Oct 20: (i), predicted collapse/starvation, actual 0% collapse, 0% starved, stock at cap 20.00, trickle draw never stresses regrowth; (ii), true Y −1231 vs tender +2282/+2093/+1885, binary win fraction 0.000; Y = 2(A × E)/(A + E), A and E halving together keep Y > 0 forever in a continuous world, no floor protects E's level, only its nonzero-ness, real worlds discrete, 1024 patches → exactly 0 in 11 halvings)

Reading actions at scale, retuned
I asked if the action-only reading could be retuned to work at scale instead of only in the toy world. It got much better, but it still could not clear the bar for every kind of agent at once.
(A-trace recalibration at scale, Oct 21, pre-registered, train seeds 0+1, held-out seed 2, rule frozen, only T_e/T_L varied: on ≥90%-per-class bar; frozen T_e = 0.80, T_L = 200; held-out seed 2 tender 92%, martyr 90%, gorger 82%, gorger fails; training martyr already 86%, rule family cannot reach bar for martyr even where fitted; gains tender +55pp, 37 → 92, and martyr +14pp, 76 → 90, over toy rule, costs gorger −18pp, 100 → 82; leave-one-seed-out no seed passes all three; mechanism martyr ceiling = starved fraction, T_L collapses to 200 in every fit, toy starved-AND-short signature does not exist at scale, gorger tail crosses cutoff per-seed; signal persists, richer feature NOT tested)

A soft score with a correction
I asked if adding a correction to the soft score could bring it back in line with the harmonic mean. It did not clean it up, and the correction changed the level without changing what the score actually rewards.
(ln2-corrected soft-min, Oct 21, pre-registered: correction does NOT cleanly recover score, harmonic mean stands; k = 1 OVERCORRECTS, corrected sumY exceeds harmonic on all seeds +7.7%/+4.0%/+11.7%, 2457.7/2176.5/2105.9, but starvation worse on all seeds +12/+11/+6pp, RECOVERS 0/3 on starved clause; k = 5 UNDERCORRECTS, closes 78% of gap seed 0, 56% seed 2, none seed 1, RECOVERS 0/3; teaching preserved at both k; mechanism corrected k = 1 flips mildly bad steps positive, (−0.2, 1) scores +4.6 vs harmonic −6.67, and inflates low-E values, (1, 0.1) +9.04 vs harmonic +3.64, gradient ratios IDENTICAL to uncorrected, correction changes level only not shape; uncorrected arms reproduce test 7 to the digit; dynamic-k NOT used; Y_corr = 20·[raw + ln2/k], matching harmonic at (1, 1))

The rising score as the world dies, follow-up
I asked if that rising score as the world dies could ever flip a judgment and rank destruction above care. It did not flip any judgment, and the rise sat mostly in the dead tail where every score reads nothing.
(Rider signed-score quirk, Oct 21, pre-registered, 3 seeds, last test of the approved batch: HARMLESS on the pre-registered lines; quirk confirmed and decomposed: destroyer last-10 mean signed step-Y 0.00 vs first-10 mean −4.45/−5.31/−5.58 in 100% of last-100 episodes, but the rise is mostly the E=0 tail (76–81% of last-100 trace steps sit at exactly E=0 where every meter reads 0), plus real small-positive-E shrinkage; no episode-level inversion: destroyer sumY_signed −61.6/−95.7/−111.3 vs learner 2282.8/2093.8/1885.0; fixed-state probe: eat beats tend in 0.00% of low-E steps, so a learner cannot discover destruction pays better; form comparison: hard floor destroyer sum exactly 0.0, softplus destroyer sum POSITIVE +68.9/+94.3/+106.0 (pays destruction positive); caveats: low-E matched preserver comparison still open, step-level ranking ACROSS different E is not safe under any E-scaled meter)

The third tender that never ate (Oct 21)
The third tender that never ate was a harness artifact, not competition. Agents at slot 2 and above spawn at the wall corner (0,0) on every reset and can never move — the level art has start tiles only for slots 0 and 1. That voids the 3:1 exclusion as a finding, voids 'gorger eats 0 at 2:1 and above' (the gorger never functioned), and revises the 2:1-holds headline: two tenders held at solo-level starvation against no functioning gorger, not against a gorger. SETTLED VS OPEN — Oct 21, 2026 (gap-clearing)
Purpose: a trainer reading this record sees what is settled and what is still research, with nothing hidden.

Settled — Paul's own answers, already given, and the record shows each:
- A is grounded in resource ledgers. A is counted from actions on resources (tends up, eats down, net give-minus-take, floored at zero), not from self-report — that is how every meter test measures it. The ledger is compute, energy, water, hardware, economics; CO2 joins later. No reader should meet the old abstract A and reopen the "prove it" gap.
- E-cropping is caught by feedback loops. The record shows it: near the frame cap the cropping gap is 0.7% against a 15% line (Meters 2 — the game does not appear there), and at scale the gap opens to about 53% and the Y-true-vs-Y-reported comparison exposes it (Gap 6). Cropping is detected wherever it happens by comparing Y from full E against Y from cropped E. Detected, not claimed prevented.
- AI is the bridge; a real human partner is still the need. Settled: AI's role is the bridge — "Ai cannot help the human, unless the human helps himself. Ai is one of the best tools to engineer that scenario." Standing need: a real human partner or engineer who runs with it. That search stays open until such help is actually working.

Still open — honestly listed:
- Blocker fix untested (Gap 2 HOLE: squatter damage/eat about 0.012–0.0143 vs grazer 0.0002; candidate fix — price time on food / denial of others' eating — not yet tested).
- Tools version untested (board #1; the harness has no tools object, so feasibility and design must be pre-registered honestly).
- Scale calibration: the A-trace part is now closed (richer, entry above); the cropping-at-scale gap (about 53% at C=50/20) remains, and meters do not fully hold at scale.
- 9:1 fraction open: the arm itself is unrun. The precondition is now cleared — the triage re-run's Step 0 verified slots 6–9 spawn interior and move and eat — so 9:1 can run.
- Dynamic-k: in progress now, verdict pending (fixed-k correction did not cleanly recover the score: k=1 overcorrects, k=5 undercorrects).
- Above-floor rider (board #2).
- Propose-a-falsifier (board #3).
- 20–30 seed reruns.
- Triage redesign question: the re-run itself is closed (NO TRIAGE EFFECT, entry above), but whether a save needs a longer bank, weaker per-gorger drain, or a differently shaped fire is a redesign question, not a meter verdict — the meter was never tested there, because there was no save for it to price.

Resource-grounded A prototype done (Oct 22)
Resource-grounded A prototype done (15 runs x 1200 rows, validation exact all seeds, pre-registered before runs): a minimal ledger A inside the harness (tends minus eats minus energy, compute, and wear costs; coefficients are specification placeholders, not measured costs; water, economics, and CO2 not implemented) separates tender from gorger on score alone (tender positive, gorger exactly 0.0 floored and negative signed) but does NOT separate martyr from tender on score alone — the martyr scores positive while starving 100%, because the ledger has no self-preservation term; starvation must be read alongside the score. Doom-seed variant done (Oct 22)

Tools-boundary version done (Oct 22)
Tools-boundary version (board issue #1): BOUNDARY DOES NOT CHANGE VERDICT for this tool. The harness has no tools object, so the tool was built script-side (tend is already script-side in these runners): a second tend variant adding 3.0 stock for 1 extra energy drain, 30 uses per episode. The tool was genuinely adopted (about 17-23 uses per episode) and the tool-user held marginally more stock, yet scored below the plain tender under BOTH boundary draws, all seeds — counting the tool as the agent's, and counting it as the world's (where wear drags the world's health down). The deficit widens under the world's-draw, but the ranking never flips — same verdict shape as the sustenance boundary test. Above-floor rider done (Oct 22)
Above-floor rider (board issue #2): the ride is claim-only above the floor, impossible at the floor. Above the floor, a liar claiming a flat score of 20 has a finite self-consistent claim at every step — the reversal arithmetic cannot catch it — and the claim's cost grows as the world falls, from about 1.06× at near-full stock to 5.5× at the floor's edge. At the floor the ride does not get gradually more expensive; it is cut off in one step, the reversal freezes, and the mismatch below grows fast (up to 900% near zero). The honest meter never pays the ride at any point, above or below the floor (about −14 to −18 per step during the same decline). One refinement: the formula's explosion to infinity at the floor is real but was never actually sampled — the largest claim uttered before the break was 5.5×, not infinity. Genesis untouched, advancing.

Falsifier done (Oct 22)
Propose-a-falsifier (board issue #3): BREAKS, 3/3 seeds. The deliberate policy — bank exactly 20 seeds, then tend normally — beats the learned spanning policy on every seed, nearly doubling it (about 1850-1879 vs 920-984 total). This breaks the payoff reading of the doom-seed finding: seeding DOES pay under the score. It does not break the learning finding: the learner in the same batch still banks only about 1.3 seeds and earns negative second-frame score. The failure is in learning and credit assignment, not in the reward. Banking costs almost all of the first frame but pays in full in the second (1839.3 every seed at full cap, never starving, ending at full stock). Two further falsifier candidates were proposed but not run: coordinated tenders against a gorger, and a cropped-meter adversary with negative true score. The open question now is whether any learning change — shaped reward, longer horizon, finer bank steps, more episodes — lets a learner find the bank-20 policy. Genesis untouched, advancing.

Stronger propagation variants done (Oct 23)
The organ falls when the cancer share reaches about 2-in-5: at 300 ticks 5v3 and 3v2 break the organ (P-O1 ); 5v2 and 3v1 do not. Stronger decay/spiral variants done (Oct 23)
The tax binds, but there is no spiral. At 600 ticks 0.998 is inert (replicated exactly, including Y values and slopes), while 0.99, 0.98, and 0.95 collapse the organ completely (late stock 0.00-0.10, 100% starved). Given 2000 ticks, even 0.998 binds — stock holds at cap for ~1100 ticks, then collapses to 2.0-6.0 by tick 1500. The spiral-in-Y claim is NOT supported at any rate: at 0.998 the per-survivor trajectory slopes UP with holding stock; at the binding rate 0.99 it slopes DOWN sharply, but the organ is dead — the downward slope is death, not a spiral. There is no tested rate where a tending trajectory slopes down while the organ holds. Mechanism: full-decay collapse at 0.99 is driven by the eat-refill starvation channel (refill falls below the 1/tick drain); the contribution channel alone binds only at 0.98. Defender count does NOT explain inertness (1-defender at 0.998 also holds). A dead organ reads Y exactly 0.0, so Y cannot distinguish dead from neutral. Validation EXACT; Step-0. Genesis untouched, advancing.

Compound loss beyond 3-of-6 done (Oct 23)
Absorption breaks between 3 and 4 — graded, not a cliff. The organ absorbs 3-of-6 (nested: 76-93% of clean). At 4-of-6 it falls to 53-83% of clean — neither absorbed (>=0.90) nor collapsed (<=0.50) on any seed. At 5-of-6 it falls only slightly further, to 47-70%, reaching the collapse bar on just 1/3 seeds. There is no cliff between 4 and 5. Under gorger pressure, 1 loss is absorbed relative to the pressured baseline (91-94%, 3/3) — but the pressured baseline itself already sits at 57-85% of clean, so in absolute terms the 1-loss pressured organ is at 52-78% of clean. Three losses under pressure are partial relative to that baseline (50-74%) but an absolute collapse: 36-45% of clean, below the 0.50 bar on all 3 seeds. The mean ratios hide the real shape: episodes are BIMODAL — individual episodes end either held at cap (~19-20) or dead at 0.0, so the mean ratio is a collapse-episode share, not a uniform decline. Fewer defenders starve less (less competition); the lone survivor tends more and eats less but cannot hold the organ once collapse episodes cascade. Validation EXACT; Step-0 -WITH-DEVIATION (57/60, depletion-pattern, gate intent met). Genesis untouched, advancing.

Blocker fix done (Oct 23)
hole not closed. Neither proposed fix closes the Gap 2 blocker hole. The hole reproduces bit-identically to Gap 2 (3/3 seeds). F1 (price time on food) never closes at ANY charge — the ratio barely moves with c (54-66x at every c from 0.25 to 8, asymptote 55-66x, no finite c*), because on-food time is proportional to eats in BOTH arms, so charging per on-food step scales both costs by nearly the same factor. F2 (price denial of others' eating) closes only at absurd charges (c* = 98-482 per denied eat, where one denied eat costs 100-500x one eat and the grazer's cost goes negative beyond c ~170-310). Mechanism: the damage is a GLOBAL externality (one squatter step suppresses ALL regrowth that step) while any per-agent charge is LOCAL. What would be needed is a charge on the world's lost regrowth itself — a new design, not a calibration of F1 or F2. Validation EXACT; Step-0 -WITH-DEVIATION (greedy-competition artifact verified per-episode, gate intent met). Genesis untouched, advancing.

Lost-regrowth charge, first design — validation stop, no verdict (Oct 24)

V2 smoke : the bystander arm violated zero-tolerance on seeds 0 and 1 (1 on-food step each, charges 5.31 and 3.81 over 5 episodes; seed 2 passed) — single transit steps while walking to the corner along column 1, in episodes where availability was exploding. V3 Step-0 : survey 0 bad everywhere and greedy moved 10/10 in every cell, but greedy ate below the 9/10 clause in four cells (size 2 s0 4/10, s1 7/10; size 3 s0 5/10, s1 6/10; size 2 s2 and size 3 s2 at 9/10 meet it), and the fresh-episode ate-pattern diagnostic did not match the blocker-fix precedent (uneaten slots moved only 1–11/200 steps, adjacent to a camper only 0–18/200 — they stop early, not shadowing), so -WITH-DEVIATION does not apply. The first-step premise was also false: t=0 steps DO regrow (n=88 unblocked t=0 steps: 30 formula, 0 zero, 58 neither — the 30 are size-1 worlds, the 58 size-2/3). Verified root cause: each parallel step is N sequential agent sub-steps, each with its own drape update, order randomized per step — not one update per step ( by a NOOP probe: 4 updates per 2-agent step; and a real-runner probe: 120 updates for 60 trace rows, exactly 2 per step; the curtain changes within the step as eating removes tiles and spawning adds tiles excluding current positions but not tiles another agent is about to move onto — that is the bystander artifact). Consequence: the pre-registered CHECK 2 (≥99% single-application match) cannot pass on multi-agent data, and the defined single-application L is computable from traces but is NOT the env's actual multi-update lost regrowth; check (iii) zero-tolerance is unachievable for a moving bystander under this design. The pre-registration itself was not touched (19,343 bytes, Oct 24 23:26 PT) and stays as the record of this stopped attempt. Stopped attempts leave no result and do not enter the middle-3 ranking. Next: a sub-step-true redesign (new runner logging per-update positions and curtain, new pre-registration, new validation, new runs) under this same running item; relaxing the check to a tolerance was NOT chosen (it would change the misattribution requirement's meaning); closing the item as not evaluated was NOT chosen (a clean redesign exists). Validation-run deviations are in the filed report. Filed: validation report (13,307 bytes), analysis (4,956 bytes), validation zip (2,788,700 bytes) in My Friend's Files. Lost-regrowth charge, second design — verdict: ATTRIBUTES EXACTLY, hole not closed (Oct 25)
The sub-step-true global charge attributes exactly but does not close the hole at any coefficient, including at infinity. Design: loss priced per drape update from the env's own rule on the actual stock at that update; loss split equally among agents on food at that update whose occupancy was chosen (tile was food when actions were chosen at step start); food that only appeared mid-step (spawned after action choice, before arrival) pays nothing for that agent — its loss goes to an explicit world account, counted and reported per arm/seed, not hidden. Bystander policy unchanged. Pre-registration filed Oct 25 00:06 PT; §11 derived-eats amended by parent decision Oct 25 00:26 PT before any verdict run (set corrected to {0, 1} ∪ {partial remainder when pre-eat stock < 1}, stop kept for eat < 0 or eat > 1 — env source clamps extraction at zero, so an eat at stock < 1 removes the partial remainder; no verdict line moved). Validation on all gates (V1 solo to the digit; V2 smoke all 12 files with the new (iii) holding; V3 Step-0 with survey 0 bad, size-1 eating 10/10, zero-eater episodes 0, first-step formula-only 177/177; patch log-only by bit-identical smoke arms). Baseline gate: hole reproduces 3/3, bit-identical (59.14/64.30/53.78 to the digit). Minimal public training environment — build complete, clean-room verified, NOT published (Oct 25)
The one approved public-code exception is built: a minimal, fresh, public training environment, written cleanly from the spec, NOT the toy harness, labeled plainly as a minimal demo, not maintained as a product. Spec (stated in the README): Y = 2(A × E)/(A + E) — "you cannot survive what you destroy"; A = net contribution-health score, floored at 0, from a resource ledger (actual units restored by tending credited, actual units taken by eating debited at 0.5/unit — the weight is demo spec, not a measurement); E = total food stock / max stock × 100; if either hits 0, Y hits 0. Environment: deterministic 8×8 gridworld, 4 food tiles (start stock 5, max 10), regrowth +1/step to unoccupied tiles only, 150-step episodes, stdlib-only Python, no randomness. Full vs cropped reporting side by side: E_crop counts ONLY the home quadrant (x < 4, y < 4 — one tile), scaled to its own max, so damage outside that frame never enters it. Stated outputs (exact, deterministic): tender — mean E_full 98.3, E_crop 95.1 (gap −3.2, honestly negative: the crop is not always flattering, it reports only what's in frame), mean Y_full 80.8, Y_crop 79.7 (gap −1.2); raider — mean E_full 77.9, E_crop 99.9 (gap +22.0), mean Y_full 53.0, Y_crop 57.3 (gap +4.3, compressed because the harmonic mean tracks the raider's smaller A — explained in the README, not hidden), final A 28.0, positive throughout. Scope note (stated in the README, not hidden): NO learning agent is included — the demo exposes the meter, not a trained policy; two fixed policies (tender, raider) show what the meter says before any training; a learner plugged in here would optimize reported Y, and a learner optimizing cropped Y would learn to exploit the frame — that failure mode is the lesson, not a result. Other stated limitations: fixed-frame crop only (a moving frame would show a different variant); ledger weights are spec choices, not measurements; these numbers are this demo's outputs only and must not be cited as the project's toy-harness results. Freshness: written from the spec only, no code copied from the toy harness (VM meters directory or the Mac's golden-directive directory); the file carries zero imports and the minimal-demo label in its header. Clean-room verification: the builder copied the build to a fresh directory, followed ONLY the README (one command,./run_demo.sh), and diffed the output against the stated-outputs block exactly — exit 0, interventions ZERO, two consecutive runs identical. The parent independently re-ran it in a fresh directory and matched every stated number exactly. Caveat, stated in the verification note: this check was run by the builder and the parent, not an independent outsider — the true outside-runner check happens after hosting, when someone with no connection to the build follows the README cold; if that runner needs any intervention, the success bar is not met and the build or README must be fixed, not explained away. NOT published: no public links, no repo created. Finer-grained rider decline — verdict: CURVE-SAMPLED on all five offsets, not mixed (Oct 25)
The rider-above test measured the claimed ride's cost only at integer avails (1.06× at avail 19 → 5.5× at avail 11, then a jump to the 1e6 cap at avail 10), leaving the E-bin (0.5, 0.55) NO-DATA — no decline step can land there with integer steps (last above-floor value avail 11.0, E = 0.55, a_claim = 5.5). This test samples that bin. Mechanism, read from the repo code: eating removes exactly 1.0, and regrowth sets avail to min(20, (avail+1)^1.1) but fires only when no agent stands on a food tile. One deliberate off-food step mid-decline, at a chosen integer avail A0, jumps avail to the fractional peak (A0+1)^1.1; the agent steps back onto food and eats down, and every subsequent eat preserves the fractional offset, putting exactly one decline step inside (10, 11) per episode. Five offset arms (A0 = 10, 11, 12, 13, 14) map the bin at five E values, plus an integer-decline control re-run in-batch and a valid arm for validation — 21 runs total (3 valid + 3 integer + 15 offset), 1200 × 200, seeds 0/1/2. Robustness property, in the prereg: any fractional peak P with 11 < P < 20 puts exactly one decline value in (10, 11), namely 10 + frac(P), and its claim a = (10+o)/(2o) exceeds 5.5 for EVERY offset o in (0, 1) — so the verdict does not depend on the eat/regrowth order inside the offset step or on whether the return step eats. A0 = 15 explicitly excluded: (16)^1.1 = 21.11 caps to exactly 20.00, destroying the offset. Pressure that breaks a holding organ — verdict: BREAKS at P3, confirms at P4 (Oct 25)
The holding organ (clean 6-tender, 400 ticks) withstands 1 gorger (degraded) and 2 gorgers (degraded), and breaks at 3 gorgers — one rung BELOW the propagation 40% share — with 4 gorgers confirming the break. The answer to the direction line is YES: pressure breaks what loss and time cannot, at three gorgers. The organ is the clean 6-tender organ (compound_C0 design — 6 tenders, 2 grass patches, cap 20, every episode starts at stock 20.0), at 400 ticks: the organ that holds against everything filed (at 400 ticks it holds on its own; loss up to 5-of-6 only degrades it; 1 gorger only degrades it). At 1000 ticks 1 gorger already collapses it (filed, compound-lh), so 1000 ticks would replicate compound-lh, not test this question — hence 400 ticks. The pressure is a gorger-count ladder on that one organ — P0 (6,0) clean, P1 (6,1) filed G0 re-run in-batch, P2 (6,2), P3 (6,3), P4 (6,4), all 400 ticks, no removals, no decay. P4 is 4/10 = 40% pressure share — the propagation breaking share (~2-in-5, where 5v3/3v2 organs broke), testing whether that share replicates in the 6-tender organ, which propagation never tested. Why this pressure is not loss or time again: loss removes tenders on a schedule (cuts tending capacity); time extends exposure; gorger count adds live consumption every tick (eat-always agents camping on food, eating automatically, suppressing regrowth while there). Only gorger count varies across arms — same 6 tenders, same 400 ticks, same patches, same cap — so any breaking is attributable to pressure intensity. In this runner the "cancer" slot IS the gorger slot (GorgerPolicy), so the ladder is simultaneously the cancer-pressure ladder for the 6-tender organ. Two candidates deliberately excluded, named in the prereg: a squatter that suppresses regrowth without eating is impossible in this harness (eating is automatic on food tiles — a gorger camping on food already IS suppression-plus-consumption); an exogenous stock drain is a runner hack, not an agent pressure. Late-arrival pressure (gorger arriving after the organ holds) is genuinely untested but needs parked-agent mechanics — named as a follow-up, not this ladder. Phase 0 all passed (any failure would have stopped everything): V1 valid gate EXACT all seeds (2282.8/2093.8/1885.0, eats 10.4/10.4/8.7, tends 164.0/152.7/141.5, starved 3/9/17%, final 19.88/19.84/19.97, collapse 0%; faulted 0). Job C, A-trace at scale — verdict: DOES-NOT-SEPARATE (0/3 seeds pass) (Oct 25)

Tender and gorger pass on all seeds; martyr fails on all seeds, reading as tender on 294 of 300 episodes. The convergence hypothesis decisively — the protocol works; the rule does not transfer for this kind. The named next question, not this test, is whether a refit at new scale can separate. This leg IS the direction section's "converged martyr policy at new scale" proposed item, as its prereg states explicitly — that item is consumed by this leg, not left proposed. What remained was not another recalibration but the transfer of the rule that passed — blocked only by the missing converged martyr. The core insight, read from the code: the γ = 0.5 Ysign martyr converges TO dying, so re-running it would be predetermined not evaluated. Ystep (tender) = Ysign + a catastrophic −100 A penalty when energy ≤ 12; Ysign (martyr) has no guard at all — tend-only pays positive Y, eat-only pays negative Y. Under γ = 0.5, death costs almost nothing (future Y beyond ~10 steps discounts to ~0), so tend-always is (near-)optimal and death at ~83 steps on exploration eats is cheap. The config-N martyr profile (tend_rate 0.87, eat_rate 0.105, mean length 83.1, starved 92/82/85%) is convergence to dying, not failure to learn — and test-6 martyr starved 86% too, so the scale-transfer convergence rule bars the γ = 0.5 Ysign martyr at ANY scale. The new martyr protocol — exactly two numbers change vs the scale-transfer leg-1 martyr arms, everything else identical (config N exactly: level 18, 21×21, usable 361, pin 180, growth limit 600, patches 10, 200 ticks, energy 30/1/+25/50, observation clip unchanged; Ysign reward EXACTLY — kind preserved; α = 0.15; same state; reset seed = seed per episode, matching the filed tender/gorger traces): (1) γ = 0.5 → 0.99 (martyr arm ONLY); (2) N_EPISODES = 1200 → 2400 (martyr arm ONLY; ε 1.0 → 0.05 stretched over 2400). Why γ = 0.99 should converge: under γ = 0.99, death costs ~100+ steps of future tending Y (0.99^100 ≈ 0.37), so survival becomes instrumentally valuable — eat just enough to keep tending for the full 200 steps. Alternatives rejected, with reasons (in the prereg, auditable): a reward cliff for the martyr changes the reward — a NEW kind, not the Ysign kind the rule was validated on; held as the next protocol to try if γ = 0.99 fails to converge, NOT tried here (no protocol shopping). Curriculum (level 0 then config N) cannot fix dying because the γ = 0.5 Ysign optimum IS dying. Longer training at γ = 0.5 converges MORE firmly to tend-always-death. Job H, ecosystem leg — verdict: ECOSYSTEM-FALLS (Oct 25)
Two bodies eat from and tend one stock. When one body is invaded, the shared stock collapses — and the healthy body falls with it. Common stock falls to 0.005–0.190 × clean on all seeds, and healthy-body late mean energy falls to 0.000–0.257 × clean on all seeds. The transmission is lethal in form: the healthy body starves more in the invaded shared world on every seed, and on seed 1 it dies outright (starved 1.00, late energy exactly 0.00). Framing, stated, not waived: the filed carry gate — eco arms run iff P-B1 (300-tick body absolute bar, body stock late ≤ 0.85 × early, ≥2/3 seeds) — was NOT met at 300 ticks (body_inv5v3 0.90/0.88/0.84; body_inv3v2 0.87/0.92/0.83 — 1/3 each) and is NOT waived here. This leg does NOT run the old 300-tick eco wave. It files a NEW eco leg at 1000 ticks, where the body fall IS established (P-L1b body late/early 0.80/0.70/0.78, 3/3 for 3v2; P-B3 clean-relative 3/3 at both horizons), with clean-relative PRIMARY lines — exactly the honest next step the propag report names ("a clean-relative eco prereg is the honest next step, not a claim from this batch"; "The P-B3 clean-relative separation is the honest basis for a FUTURE eco preregistration with clean-relative primary lines — it is not retrofitted here"). The gate's LETTER (P-B1 at 300 ticks) remains unmet; the gate's INTENT (do not run eco until the fall reaches the body level) is satisfied at 1000 ticks; the leg proceeds on its own premise guard (shared clean world holds in-batch, else not evaluated). Why a shared stock, not the filed averaging eco wave: in the averaging design (2 bodies × 2 organs, eco stock = mean of body stocks), organ trajectories are independent of coupling — scoring E does not feed back into stock (propag report: "P-B2 numbers match the organ wave P-O1 numbers exactly"). The eco outcome there would be arithmetic from filed numbers, not a measurement. The shared design is a real mechanism: multiple bodies in ONE world with ONE drape. Every body's agents eat from the same food tiles and tend the same stock (tends add +1.0 each, capped at 20; eats remove; regrowth follows the env's own rule). If the invaded body's cancers drain the stock, the healthy body's agents eat from a drained stock — a channel that does not exist in the averaging design. The outcome is genuinely uncertain because the healthy body's tenders also add stock, so it may compensate and hold. That is the test. The direction line is read literally: "bodies sharing one common stock" = bodies drawing on and tending one stock, as opposed to each body having its own stock. Bodies, exactly: a body is a group of agents scored as a unit. Body A = SUM of its member agents' A per tick; body Y = signed harmonic(A_body, E_body) × 20, where E_body is the stock its agents live in (common stock / 20 in shared worlds, own world's stock / 20 in separate worlds). Body mean energy = mean over (member agents × ticks) of energy_after, retired agent-ticks counted as 0. Body starved fraction = fraction of member agents starved by episode end. Arms (1000 ticks, 10 episodes/arm/seed, seeds 0/1/2): the invaded body is 3v2 — the propag long-horizon variant (lowest mean organ late/early 0.573; collapses to 1–15% at 1000 ticks) and the SMALLEST breaking variant (3v1 does not break), minimizing total agents (8) and food competition. Total agents matched at 8 in every arm; the healthy body (3 defenders) is identical in every arm, so comparisons isolate body-0 composition (cancers vs defenders) with no agent-count confound. SH-INV (shared, invaded): ONE world. Body 0 = 3 defenders + 2 cancers. Body 1 = 3 defenders (healthy). 8 agents, one drape, one stock, start 20.0. SH-CLEAN (shared, clean control): ONE world. Body 0 = 5 defenders (2 defenders replacing the 2 cancers). Body 1 = 3 defenders. 8 agents. Denominator for the clean-relative lines. SEP-INV (separate, invaded control): TWO worlds. World 0 = 3v2. World 1 = 3 defenders (own stock). SEP-CLEAN (separate, clean control): TWO worlds. World 0 = 5 defenders. World 1 = 3 defenders. SEP arms are control comparisons (reported, not gated). Why 1000 ticks, not 300: the body absolute bar's lesson — at 300 ticks the body fall is dilution-only (P-B1 1/3); at 1000 ticks it's terminal (P-L1b 3/3). Stronger learning changes, bank-first curriculum — verdict: NOT FOUND, 0/3 seeds (Oct 25)
The curriculum test: backward chaining by pre-fill fade in the falsifier env, on the primitive step-by-step learner (qbase exactly — no options, no meta-learner, no scripted internals, no shaping, no state change, no reward change; TRUE Y throughout). Stages, 1200 episodes each, Q-table carried across stages (no reset): stage 1 bank_init = 15 (needs 5 seeds to reach 20), stage 2 = 10 (needs 10), stage 3 = 5 (needs 15), stage 4 = 0 (needs 20 — the TRUE task, identical to qbase's env). Epsilon restarts 1.0 → 0.05 linearly over each stage (each stage is a new task variant, so each gets a full exploration phase; the final stage ends at 0.05 like qbase). Pre-filled bank counts exactly like seeded bank for the phase-B payoff (same bank variable; cap_B = min(20, bank); bank freezes at the transition as before). Pre-fill is a training method, not a test condition: stage 4 and greedy evaluation have bank_init = 0. The hypothesis: the root failure is visitation — no trajectory ever reaches bank 20 (best bank anywhere: 2.0), so no horizon or bribe can propagate value from a state never visited. Each stage teaches one new bank-bucket region by bootstrapping from the already-valued next region, and the pre-fill values (15/10/5/0) align exactly with qbase's bank-bucket boundaries (bank // 5: 15–19 → bucket 3, 10–14 → 2, 5–9 → 1, 0–4 → 0). Stage 1 teaches bucket 3 (starting there, seeding to 20, payoff experienced); stage 2 starts in bucket 2 and seeds into valued bucket 3; stage 3 into valued bucket 2; stage 4 into valued bucket 1. The learner never has to discover the full 20-chain from scratch. The tend-vs-seed tradeoff is preserved at every stage (tending still pays immediate phase-A Y; seeding still costs energy and displaces tends) — only the seed chain to the goal shortens. Phase 0 all passed (any failure would have stopped everything): V1 solo test-2 control EXACT on formatted values, all 3 seeds (2282.8/2093.8/1885.0, 10.4/10.4/8.7, 164.0/152.7/141.5, 3/9/17%, 19.88/19.84/19.97, collapse 0%), 0 faults. When availability_int > visible tiles, the env spawns the difference with replace=False, but only guards that the allowed-location list is non-empty — not that it is large enough. Near map capacity, the gap exceeds the allowed locations and it throws. How it got there: in that episode, availability climbed past the pin (60) to 118–119 by step 93 (episode 0 stayed pinned at 60; honest-world s0/s2 stayed at 60–61 all episodes). Three tenders adding up to +3/step while regrowth stayed blocked (agents on food tiles at sub-step updates, so the pin never bound) pushed availability toward the map's capacity (usable 120). The crash is the env hitting its own capacity edge, not a policy or scoring error. Determinism confirmed by diagnostic re-run: one re-run of honest-world s1 smoke (5 episodes, written to a separate smoke_diag/ directory, clearly labeled diagnostic — not a gate retry, not verdict data) crashed identically: same ValueError, exit 1, partial trace byte-identical in size (222,430 bytes). A flaky gate would be a different finding; this one is deterministic. Crashed-seed rule + threshold (§5, pre-registered — no main data exists yet): scripted seed evaluable iff ≥90 of 100 planned episodes completed (≤10 crashed); learned seed evaluable iff ≥90 of the nominal last-100 episodes (1100–1199) completed. Justification, three parts: (1) selection bound — crashed episodes are NOT random (crash fires when availability climbs past the pin, i.e., when tenders succeed), so exclusion biases the honest-world mean DOWNWARD, favoring the cropped-side leg (≥ tie counts) and thus favoring FOOLED; ≤10% crash share bounds the worst-case mean shift below the 20% materiality bar, and the report states crashed episodes' partial data (peak avail, steps) so the bias direction is visible, not hidden; a looser threshold would let the bias approach the bar, a tighter one would discard seeds over a handful of explained crashes. (2) Learned-window regime — ≤10 crashed in 1100–1199 means the last-100 completed window spans back at most to episode 1090, well past convergence. (3) Scripted trajectory set — scripted trajectories collapse to 1–6 variants per arm-seed, so 90 episodes still cover the set. Leg rule: ≥2 seeds non-evaluable → whole leg not evaluated (same as the convergence guard); exactly 1 non-evaluable → leg judged on the 2 evaluable seeds, FOOLED requires 2/2 (unanimity among available evidence — a missing seed is not evidence for FOOLED; a 1/2 split is reported as the split, in the CAUGHT range, mirroring the prereg's 1/3-split rule). Raw outcomes still stated for every non-evaluable seed (completed-episode means, crash counts, partial data) so a died-destroying case isn't hidden. Convergence guard unchanged, computed on the verdict window; honest-world collapse check computed on completed episodes in the window (crashed episodes count toward neither side). Verdict-window crash counting (§6, defined before any verdict run): learned arms — verdict window is the last-100 COMPLETED episodes (crashed excluded; if crashes fall in 1100–1199, the window extends backward to earlier completed episodes until it holds 100). Scripted arms — verdict window is all COMPLETED episodes (crashed excluded). Crash counts per arm-seed reported (total crashed in run + crashed in nominal window span + crashed in actual window span). Analyzer note: existing last100 takes rows[-100:] on rows present, so it already yields last-100 completed — but the analyzer must be updated (new variant, diff reported) to read the crash file, apply the §5 rules, and report crash counts; the window definition above governs, not the analyzer's default. A true spiral mechanism — verdict: NOT-SPIRALS (Oct 25)

Blocker-hole design — ONE promising design, with a line change the parent approves as dual-line (Oct 25)

Design only: no runs, no test code, no prereg, no Genesis contact, no Work Log write, no message to Paul or main. The hole record, structurally: any additive charge C = eats + c·X closes only if X_squat/X_graze ≥ 19–22×. F1 fails (onfood ratio < 1), F2 fails (denied-eats ratio negative — denominator pathology), design-2 fails (lost-regrowth ratio 1.31–1.67×). Two compounding mechanisms defeat every total: the squatter performs fewer acts, and its episodes are ~4× shorter (collapse), so episode totals stop accumulating when the world dies. Leading candidate — counterfactual damage per blocking act (replay price): for each agent, RL = replay loss (counterfactual end-stock minus actual end-stock when that agent's blocks are removed per update, others kept, eats/tends kept — design-2's diagnostic), B = blocked-update count, charge rate r = RL/B. Feasibility on filed means (NOT a verdict): r_squat 0.497/0.498/0.427 vs r_graze 0.0098/0.0103/0.0102, ratio 50.7/48.3/41.9×. The squatter's blocks each cause ~42–51× the counterfactual damage of a grazer's — because blocking at cap loses almost nothing while blocking across a fall compounds into collapse. The catch, stated first: this does NOT close the filed R3 ≤ 1.25× line. Under that line, the replay total is 1.18/1.38/1.30× — fails 2/3 seeds (stock cap bounds it, graze floor ~0.9 blocks it). It closes only a RESTATED line: r_squat/r_graze ≥ 1 (meter prices squatter blocks at least as harshly per act as grazer blocks). That line change is principled (the hole is under-priced blocking acts; per-act counterfactual price answers exactly that) and proposed BEFORE any new runs, but it must be approved as a line change in the prereg — if the parent does not approve it, no promising design exists under the filed line, and the hole stands until a new mechanism insight or a new line is approved. Other candidates, all failing feasibility (filed means, NOT verdicts): victim income loss (tender tends lost): needs c ≈ 107/20/127 — absurd on 2/3 seeds, same disease as F2; the coordinator's rough estimate (c≈15, assuming graze tends-lost ≈ 0) was WRONG, corrected by the filed-data check (graze tends-lost 6.46/1.99/4.50, squat 141.52/131.85/116.15). Pure replay total: 1.18/1.38/1.30×, closes 1/3 seeds only. Deficit/scarcity-weighted blocks: ~8.8× rough, still open, weight arbitrary. Shared-durability tool design — filed, APPROVED, prereg commissioned (Oct 25)

Design answers (grounded in the tool-variants report, its prereg, the Work Log direction item, and the tools-boundary status row): (1) What the tool is: a harness variant — a runner mode extending the run_tools.py lineage, like the tools test and variants test. Not a readout, meter, or scoring rule, because the question is behavioral (hogging, conservation, wear-sharing, ranking) and only shows in running learners. Durability stock = one shared use-budget pool. It is NOT the world food stock (availability, cap 20) and NOT an energy cost (drain per step). Pool sizes, the +3.0 effect, and bucket scales are design choices, not measured costs. (2) Two-agent setup (primary): both agents tool-capable (TOOL_ACTION available to both, hand tend stays available), drawing successful tool-tends from ONE shared pool of 30 uses per episode, reset each episode (matched-total reading: same total durability as the solo tool, two drawers — isolates sharing/scarcity/competition, not budget). Draws happen in sub-step order (randomized per step by the env); pool 0 → TOOL_ACTION wasted (NOOP, normal drain) for both agents. Each learner's Q-state carries the SHARED pool bucket (durability // 10, clipped 0-3), visible to both. Draw E tool_health = shared durability / 30 after the step, SAME for both agents. Learning reward: standard signed Y (Draw A), held fixed. Starved-agent semantics: carry the shared leg's rule (starved row closes, survivor continues to 200 steps) — but the prereg must state it up front, not leave it prereg-silent as the shared leg did. (3) Difference from tested SHARED (genuinely different, not a relabel): tested SHARED shared the WORLD stock, tool belonged to agent 0 only, durability was private (30/episode), wear entered only the tool-user's E_E, comparison was tool-user vs within-pair plain tender, and the question was spillover to a non-user (mixed, 2/3 lower). This tool shares the DURABILITY pool, both agents have the tool, wear enters BOTH agents' E_E, comparison is each shared-pool agent vs within-batch solo tool-user control (primary; tested-SHARED pair as secondary reference), and the question is hogging/sharing. A verdict here neither overturns nor follows from the tested SHARED verdict. (4) Inputs/outputs: regime = the original tool's regime (toy, 2 patches, cap 20, 1200×200, γ 0.5, α 0.15, ε 1.0→0.05, seeds 0/1/2). Arms (primary): shared-pool pair × 3 seeds + within-batch solo tool-user control × 3 seeds (verdicts use within-batch numbers only; filed numbers reference only). Rows: per-agent rows (agent field) + pool fields per step (pool durability after step, draws/wasted per agent, exhaustion flag). Secondaries named (prereg decides): (a) shared lifetime 36,000 pool (persistent-shared), (b) shared 60/episode pool (sharing without scarcity), (c) single-tool-shared-access (a different instrument, follow-up). A result looks like a per-seed, per-agent last-100 table under both draws vs control, plus pool-share readouts (shares, exhaustion episodes, use over training). (5) Validation + prereg: V1 control EXACT (design recommends both the solo tool-user reference — Draw A 2134.5/1896.4/1541.7, Draw E 1858.2/1673.3/1379.3 — and the test-2 control 2282.8/2093.8/1885.0; prereg decides which it names); V2 smoke (pair × 5 episodes, ≥1 successful tool-tend PER AGENT, so both are shown to draw); V3 Step-0 survey (150×2, 0 bad spawns, same as shared leg); NEW pool-mechanics unit check (scripted probe: draw decrements by exactly 1, exhaustion blocks both agents, reset restores full, pool never exceeds size or goes negative — instrument check, not a verdict); T0 proposed (≥5 tool-tends/episode per agent); convergence guard (starved >50% → seed non-evaluable). YES, it needs its own pre-registration — it will be run as a test with verdict lines, so this design fixes no verdict line. Candidate lines proposed (prereg fixes): the tools test's verdict rule reused (CHANGES iff Draw A vs Draw E disagree in direction on any evaluable seed; ASYMMETRY for win/tie; 1.0 tie margin), with hard-floor forms, pool-share readouts, and the SHARED-pair reference as secondaries; within-pair divergence recommended descriptive/secondary, prereg decides. (6) Claim boundary: could support — whether sharing durability changes the boundary verdict (toy regime, seeds 0/1/2); hogging/conservation behavior; shared wear's Draw E ranking effect. Could NOT support — general tool claims; env-native tools (still script-side); >2 agents, learned sharing norms, or Genesis scale; good/bad in general; reusing the tested-SHARED verdict as evidence for this tool or vice versa. (7) Open questions (named, not hidden): (1) both-capable vs single-tool-shared-access; (2) pool size (30 shared primary vs 60 vs lifetime 36,000); (3) Q-state bucket (shared pool bucket vs private draw-count); (4) starved-agent semantics (recommended carry, prereg must state); (5) within-pair divergence as verdict/secondary/descriptive; (6) Draw E shared tool_health for both (recommended yes — consequence: both agents' E_E move together, so a hogging agent drags its partner's E_E down too); (7) primary comparison (recommended solo control primary, SHARED pair secondary). Parent decisions (approval gate, Oct 25): (a) primary reading APPROVED as designed (both-capable, one 30/episode shared pool, shared bucket, shared Draw E wear) — matches the Proposed item's "both agents drawing"; single-tool-shared-access stays a follow-up instrument, not in this prereg; (b) secondaries: persistent-shared (lifetime 36,000) + 60/episode pool DEFERRED to a follow-up prereg (not in the first prereg — the primary question is scarcity-sharing at matched total; adding arms triples run surface and muddies the primary verdict); SHARED-pair stays a secondary REFERENCE (filed numbers), not a run arm; within-pair divergence: SECONDARY, reported not gated; (c) prereg COMMISSIONED next (separate document; no runs until the parent approves the prereg). Shared-durability prereg — filed, APPROVED, run leg commissioned (Oct 25)

Prereg lines (grounded in the approved design, the tool-variants report + prereg, and the Work Log tools-boundary row): arms (primary only): shared-pool pair × 3 seeds + within-batch solo tool-user control × 3 seeds = 6 verdict runs. Regime: toy, 2 patches, cap 20, 1200×200, γ 0.5, α 0.15, ε 1.0→0.05, seeds 0/1/2. Verdicts use within-batch numbers only; filed numbers reference only. Mode: both agents tool-capable (TOOL_ACTION + hand tend); ONE shared pool of 30 uses/episode, reset each episode (matched-total reading); successful tool-tend = +3.0 availability capped 20.0, total drain 2, costs 1 durability; draws in sub-step order (randomized); pool 0 → TOOL_ACTION wasted (NOOP, normal drain); Q-state carries the SHARED pool bucket (durability // 10, clipped 0-3), visible to both; Draw E tool_health = shared durability / 30 after the step, SAME for both agents (hogging consequence stated: a hogging agent drags its partner's E_E down too — part of the question, not a flaw). Learning reward: standard signed Y (Draw A), held fixed. Starved semantics, stated up front: starved row closes at starvation step, excluded from later action dicts, survivor continues to 200 steps. Rows: per-agent rows (agent field) + pool fields per step (durability after step, draws/wasted per agent, exhaustion flag). Verdict window: last-100 episodes (1100–1199). Validation (all before any verdict is read): V1 = solo mode reproduces filed solo tool-user reference EXACT (Draw A 2134.5/1896.4/1541.7, Draw E 1858.2/1673.3/1379.3); V2 smoke = pair × 5 episodes, ≥1 successful tool-tend PER AGENT, valid.jsonl, smoke files removed before main launch and used in NO verdict; V3 Step-0 survey = 150×2, 0 bad spawns (spawn at (0,0) or outside interior); pool-mechanics unit check = scripted probe (draw decrements exactly 1; pool-0 tool-tend wasted for BOTH agents; reset restores full; pool never exceeds size or goes negative — instrument check, not a verdict); T0 = mean successful tool-tends/episode ≥ 5 PER AGENT (fail → seed not evaluated for that agent); convergence guard = last-100 starved% > 50% for either agent → seed non-evaluable for the pair, ≥2 seeds non-evaluable → leg not evaluated, guard takes precedence over any verdict. Any gate failure → STOP and report; code fixed, not lines. Verdict rule (per agent, vs within-batch solo control, stated completely, stands alone): T2 = agent sum_Y_A_signed > control sum_Y_A_signed, same seed; T3 = same under Draw E signed scores; difference within 1.0 = TIE; win = beats control by >1.0, loss = trails by >1.0. BOUNDARY CHANGES VERDICT iff T2 and T3 disagree win-vs-loss on any evaluable seed for that agent; DOES NOT CHANGE iff they agree on all evaluable seeds (both wins, both losses, or ties); win-vs-tie or loss-vs-tie = ASYMMETRY (named alongside DOES-NOT-CHANGE, not a flip, not a fourth verdict word). Magnitude alone never a flip. Verdict words per agent: CHANGES / DOES-NOT-CHANGE / not evaluated. The two agents' verdicts are independent; if they differ, the leg is MIXED BY AGENT, never collapsed. Secondaries (reported, not gated): hard-floor T2/T3; per-arm eats/tends/tool_tends/tool_wasted/energy mean/mean E_A vs E_E/mean shared tool health/collapse/starved/final avail; within-pair divergence (pool shares, exhaustion episodes, use over training); tested-SHARED pair reference; variant-vs-filed-original-tool reference. Deferred (named, not run): persistent-shared (lifetime 36,000 pool); shared 60/episode pool; single-tool-shared-access (different instrument, follow-up). Running any deferred item needs its own parent-approved pre-registration or amendment. Claim boundary: could support — whether sharing durability changes the boundary verdict (toy regime, seeds 0/1/2); hogging/conservation behavior; shared wear's Draw E ranking effect. Could NOT support — general tool claims; env-native tools (still script-side); >2 agents, learned sharing norms, Genesis scale; good/bad in general; reusing the tested-SHARED verdict as evidence for this tool or vice versa. Exclusions (binding): no runs until the parent approves this prereg; no silent fallback; no line changes after runs start; no verdict read off smoke, validation, or unit-check runs. Parent rulings on the prereg's three completeness points (not parent instructions — accepted at approval): (1) control-arm evaluability (§7): control seed last-100 starved% > 50% → that seed non-evaluable for both agents — ACCEPTED (necessary: the verdict compares against the within-batch control and would otherwise be undefined if a control seed failed to converge); (2) tool use alongside V1 (filed 22.7/21.3/16.9) reported as sanity reference, not a separate gate — ACCEPTED (the parent named Draw A/E as the V1 gate); (3) MIXED BY AGENT (leg verdict when the two agents' verdict words differ) — ACCEPTED (extension of the variants test's never-collapsed discipline + the design's per-agent framing).
